item: A full-suite run as root no longer turns /dev/null into a regular file, and the plan and out-of-memory tests pass on SQLite 3.53.1 as well as the older one
summary: First full-suite run on a second SQLite (3.53.1; 28338 passed, 5 failed, 120 skipped, 5749 s). Two tests (three registries) used Path(os.devnull) as a DamageRegistry store: the registry reads its store and then os.replace-s its record over it, which a non-root user cannot do in /dev (swallowed) and root can, so a root run left /dev/null a regular file holding the registry JSON and a distant test (stdin=DEVNULL) read it. The stores are tmp_path files; a new last-sorting file scans tests/, src/ and scripts/ for the null device (os.devnull through os, os.path, posixpath or ntpath under any alias, from-imports, getattr) and for whole-string /dev/<name> constants, str or bytes, as a path (allowlist with reasons, stale entries fail; what it cannot see is stated and pinned), proves with a unix socket that the registry replaces any node at its store path, and fails at the end of a serial run if /dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/random, /dev/urandom or (where present) /dev/full is not a character device. test_browse_plan reads the meaning of a tie-only sort (RIGHT PART on 3.45.1, LAST TERM and LAST n TERMS on 3.50.4 and 3.53.1; 3.46 to 3.49 not measured) instead of SQLite's words and proves its helper on the running library; the FTS5 out-of-memory test accepts the row (3.45.1) and the empty-MemoryError (3.53.1) shapes and keeps the verdict strictly unchecked. A fake that raises an empty MemoryError pins the raised shape on every SQLite, as the row fakes already pinned the other. Product code unchanged. Mutants killed: 36 of 36 (31 on the scan, the canary, the premise, the plan helper and the reverted pages-test store; 5 on the out-of-memory shapes and the reverted damage-test store).
